R2B-bear-backcountry-0001.name: 200 m N of Vancouver River
R2B-bear-backcountry-0001.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R2B-bear-backcountry-0001.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed paved road

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2011 (15 years old), right here: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2023 (fire V53097), 370 m NW: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
SE facing slope, 11 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Vancouver River 200 m S: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from District of Squamish, about 70 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 49.91715, -123.86556, pull off on an unnamed paved road. Map links below.
Walk: 6.3 km E, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 418 m, about 169 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 220 m SE of the spot at 249 m (49.93318, -123.7803). Water: Vancouver River 20 m N (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 2-5, Region 2. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-09, closures 2026-10-16.
R2B-bear-backcountry-0001.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 2-5: about 347 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.10 days per square km, middle third of BC MUs; access: more than 5 km from a drivable road. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

R2B-deer-backcountry-0006.name: 1.1 km N of Treat Creek
R2B-deer-backcountry-0006.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R2B-deer-backcountry-0006.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed paved road

evidence.t: Deer here are black tailed deer, the coast form of mule deer: the synopsis calls them "mule (black-tailed) deer" (99%, Rule Book: Region 2 Lower Mainland).
Mule deer winter range u-2-011 unit JR 22 (official), 30 m W. Counts from October.
Cutblock harvested 2007 (19 years old), 390 m E.
Habitat zone Coastal Western Hemlock (CWHdm2): coast forest, where black tailed deer are among the most common large mammals (95%) and use logged ground often (80%) (lesson: Wet forests).
W facing slope, 15 degrees: sun melts snow first.

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).
